title: Horton v. California (1990)
key_points: Holding: Plain view seizure is allowed when the officer is lawfully in the viewing location, the item's incriminating nature is immediately apparent, and the officer has lawful access; discovery need not be inadvertent.
officer_notes: Scenario: While lawfully executing a warrant for stolen jewelry, you see a handgun used in the robbery on a dresser.
Takeaway: NJ adopted this approach in State v. Gonzales, 227 N.J. 77 (2016).
